								<h2>2026 ATP China Open Schedule of Play: Daily Beijing Match Schedule and Tournament Guide</h2>
<p>LINK: <a href="https://www.protennislive.com/posting/2026/747/op.pdf" target="_blank" rel="noopener">China Open Schedule</a> | <a href="https://www.protennislive.com/posting/2026/329/op.pdf" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Japan Open Schedule</a></p>
<p data-start="681" data-end="816">The 2026 <a href="https://www.atptour.com/en/tournaments/beijing/747/overview" target="_blank" rel="noopener">ATP</a> China Open will bring one of the strongest men’s fields of the Asian Swing to Beijing from September 30 through October 6.</p>
<p data-start="818" data-end="1050">Defending champion <a href="https://tennisconnected.com/sinner-withdraws-from-2026-cincinnati-open/">Jannik Sinner </a>has withdrawn from the ATP 500 tournament due to an ongoing knee injury. Six-time winner Novak Djokovic, reigning Roland Garros champion Alexander Zverev, Felix Auger-Aliassime, Alex de Minaur, Flavio Cobolli and Daniil Medvedev will highlight the field. </p>
<p data-start="1052" data-end="1207">Main-draw matches will be played over seven days at Beijing’s National Tennis Center, concluding with the singles and doubles finals on Tuesday, October 6.</p>

<p data-start="16647" data-end="16670"><strong data-start="16647" data-end="16670">Anticipated rounds:</strong></p>
<ul data-start="16672" data-end="16723">
<li data-section-id="rl5vsr" data-start="16672" data-end="16697">WTA singles first round</li>
<li data-section-id="6cz9as" data-start="16698" data-end="16723">WTA doubles first round</li>
</ul>
<h2 data-section-id="vsms03" data-start="16725" data-end="16775">Friday, October 2: First Round and Second Round</h2>
<p data-start="16777" data-end="16865">The final opening-round matches are expected to be completed as the second round begins.</p>
<p data-start="16867" data-end="17069">This is when some of the leading seeds could make their first appearances. Sabalenka, Rybakina, Gauff, Swiatek and Anisimova will each face an opponent who has already played—and won—a match in Beijing.</p>
<p data-start="17071" data-end="17155">That dynamic can make the first appearance difficult for the highest-ranked players.</p>
<p data-start="17157" data-end="17180"><strong data-start="17157" data-end="17180">Anticipated rounds:</strong></p>
<ul data-start="17182" data-end="17260">
<li data-section-id="rl5vsr" data-start="17182" data-end="17207">WTA singles first round</li>
<li data-section-id="13s90fl" data-start="17208" data-end="17234">WTA singles second round</li>
<li data-section-id="6cz9as" data-start="17235" data-end="17260">WTA doubles first round</li>
</ul>
<h2 data-section-id="mtvllx" data-start="17262" data-end="17306">Saturday, October 3: Second-Round Matches</h2>
<p data-start="17308" data-end="17391">The second round will continue with a full schedule of singles and doubles matches.</p>
<p data-start="17393" data-end="17575">The expanded draw means several leading contenders could be in action on the same day. Former Beijing champions Gauff, Swiatek, Osaka and Anisimova will all be attempting to advance.</p>
<p data-start="17577" data-end="17600"><strong data-start="17577" data-end="17600">Anticipated rounds:</strong></p>
<ul data-start="17602" data-end="17654">
<li data-section-id="13s90fl" data-start="17602" data-end="17628">WTA singles second round</li>
<li data-section-id="6cz9as" data-start="17629" data-end="17654">WTA doubles first round</li>
</ul>
<h2 data-section-id="1yatatl" data-start="17656" data-end="17706">Sunday, October 4: Second Round and Third Round</h2>
<p data-start="17708" data-end="17820">The remaining second-round matches should be completed before the tournament moves further into the third round.</p>
<p data-start="17822" data-end="17989">This is where the draw begins to tighten. Seeded players can encounter experienced hard-court opponents who possess enough power or defensive skill to create an upset.</p>
<p data-start="17991" data-end="18014"><strong data-start="17991" data-end="18014">Anticipated rounds:</strong></p>
<ul data-start="18016" data-end="18106">
<li data-section-id="13s90fl" data-start="18016" data-end="18042">WTA singles second round</li>
<li data-section-id="jmob8i" data-start="18043" data-end="18068">WTA singles third round</li>
<li data-section-id="y2rd24" data-start="18069" data-end="18106">WTA doubles first and second rounds</li>
</ul>
<h2 data-section-id="1qn63dy" data-start="18108" data-end="18148">Monday, October 5: Third-Round Action</h2>
<p data-start="18150" data-end="18202">Third-round matches will dominate Monday’s schedule.</p>
<p data-start="18204" data-end="18403">Players reaching this stage will be competing for places in the round of 16. The quality of the field means potential matchups between Grand Slam champions could arrive well before the quarterfinals.</p>
<p data-start="18405" data-end="18513">Late-season ranking points and qualification for the WTA Finals will add further importance to every result.</p>
<p data-start="18515" data-end="18538"><strong data-start="18515" data-end="18538">Anticipated rounds:</strong></p>
<ul data-start="18540" data-end="18592">
<li data-section-id="jmob8i" data-start="18540" data-end="18565">WTA singles third round</li>
<li data-section-id="ejehq6" data-start="18566" data-end="18592">WTA doubles second round</li>
</ul>
<h2 data-section-id="1hda12i" data-start="18594" data-end="18644">Tuesday, October 6: Third Round and Round of 16</h2>
<p data-start="18646" data-end="18738">The singles competition is expected to transition from the third round into the round of 16.</p>
<p data-start="18740" data-end="18971">Sabalenka and Rybakina’s first-strike tennis should become increasingly important as the opposition improves. Gauff and Swiatek may have an advantage in longer, more physical matches because of their movement and returning ability.</p>
<p data-start="18973" data-end="18996"><strong data-start="18973" data-end="18996">Anticipated rounds:</strong></p>
<ul data-start="18998" data-end="19076">
<li data-section-id="jmob8i" data-start="18998" data-end="19023">WTA singles third round</li>
<li data-section-id="1v94bf3" data-start="19024" data-end="19049">WTA singles round of 16</li>
<li data-section-id="ejehq6" data-start="19050" data-end="19076">WTA doubles second round</li>
</ul>
<h2 data-section-id="1d2oeuw" data-start="19078" data-end="19114">Wednesday, October 7: Round of 16</h2>
<p data-start="19116" data-end="19181">The remaining quarterfinal places should be decided on Wednesday.</p>
<p data-start="19183" data-end="19411">A field containing the full Top 10 creates the possibility of outstanding fourth-round matches. Anisimova will be attempting to keep her title defence alive, while 2025 finalist Noskova will try to make another deep Beijing run.</p>
<p data-start="19413" data-end="19436"><strong data-start="19413" data-end="19436">Anticipated rounds:</strong></p>
<ul data-start="19438" data-end="19491">
<li data-section-id="1v94bf3" data-start="19438" data-end="19463">WTA singles round of 16</li>
<li data-section-id="1d2jvmv" data-start="19464" data-end="19491">WTA doubles quarterfinals</li>
</ul>
<h2 data-section-id="1pukr5k" data-start="19493" data-end="19544">Thursday, October 8: Singles Quarterfinals Begin</h2>
<p data-start="19546" data-end="19616">The first singles quarterfinals are expected to be played on Thursday.</p>
<p data-start="19618" data-end="19762">The WTA China Open commonly divides its quarterfinal schedule across two days, allowing featured matches to receive prominent stadium placement.</p>
<p data-start="19764" data-end="19874">By this stage, every remaining player will have adjusted to the conditions and accumulated several match wins.</p>
<p data-start="19876" data-end="19899"><strong data-start="19876" data-end="19899">Anticipated rounds:</strong></p>
<ul data-start="19901" data-end="19956">
<li data-section-id="eyzudk" data-start="19901" data-end="19928">WTA singles quarterfinals</li>
<li data-section-id="1d2jvmv" data-start="19929" data-end="19956">WTA doubles quarterfinals</li>
</ul>
<h2 data-section-id="zbd7d6" data-start="19958" data-end="20010">Friday, October 9: Singles Quarterfinals Continue</h2>
<p data-start="20012" data-end="20065">The final semifinalists will be determined on Friday.</p>
<p data-start="20067" data-end="20305">Potential meetings between Sabalenka, Rybakina, Gauff and Swiatek would carry major ranking and year-end championship implications. Andreeva, Noskova, Pegula, Anisimova and Paolini will also expect to contend for places in the final four.</p>
<p data-start="20307" data-end="20330"><strong data-start="20307" data-end="20330">Anticipated rounds:</strong></p>
<ul data-start="20332" data-end="20384">
<li data-section-id="eyzudk" data-start="20332" data-end="20359">WTA singles quarterfinals</li>
<li data-section-id="1oc7b41" data-start="20360" data-end="20384">WTA doubles semifinals</li>
</ul>
<h2 data-section-id="977szv" data-start="20386" data-end="20433">Saturday, October 10: WTA Singles Semifinals</h2>
<p data-start="20435" data-end="20505">Both women’s singles semifinals are expected to be played on Saturday.</p>
<p data-start="20507" data-end="20693">At this stage, serving efficiency and physical recovery become particularly important. The semifinalists will have already completed several matches during a demanding 12-day tournament.</p>
<p data-start="20695" data-end="20770">The doubles championship match may also be scheduled for the final weekend.</p>
<p data-start="20772" data-end="20795"><strong data-start="20772" data-end="20795">Anticipated rounds:</strong></p>
<ul data-start="20797" data-end="20855">
<li data-section-id="144de32" data-start="20797" data-end="20821">WTA singles semifinals</li>
<li data-section-id="cg3228" data-start="20822" data-end="20855">WTA doubles semifinals or final</li>
</ul>
<h2 data-section-id="1evvu36" data-start="20857" data-end="20900">Sunday, October 11: WTA China Open Final</h2>
<p data-start="20902" data-end="20969">The women’s singles champion will be crowned on Sunday, October 11.</p>
<p data-start="20971" data-end="21170">Anisimova will attempt to become the first player since the tournament’s return to successfully defend the title. Gauff, Swiatek and Osaka are the other former Beijing champions in the initial field.</p>
<p data-start="21172" data-end="21276">The winner will collect 1,000 ranking points and one of the most significant trophies of the WTA season.</p>
<p data-start="21278" data-end="21299"><strong data-start="21278" data-end="21299">Scheduled rounds:</strong></p>
<ul data-start="21301" data-end="21364">
<li data-section-id="15d3pqn" data-start="21301" data-end="21320">WTA singles final</li>
<li data-section-id="y8t69a" data-start="21321" data-end="21364">WTA doubles final, if not played Saturday</li>
</ul>
<h2 data-section-id="ohil14" data-start="21366" data-end="21419">When Is the WTA China Open Order of Play Released?</h2>
<p data-start="21421" data-end="21585">The official order of play is generally released on the evening before each day’s matches. It will list every confirmed matchup, court assignment and starting time.</p>
<p data-start="21587" data-end="21733">Beijing uses China Standard Time, which is <strong data-start="21630" data-end="21639">UTC+8</strong>. International viewers should check their local time difference before the beginning of play.</p>
<p data-start="21735" data-end="22014">The official WTA page currently confirms that the <a class="decorated-link" href="https://www.wtatennis.com/tournaments/china-open/order-of-play?utm_source=chatgpt.com" target="_new" rel="noopener" data-start="21785" data-end="21880">2026 China Open order of play</a> has not yet been published. The schedule above is a round-by-round tournament guide and will remain subject to official confirmation.</p>

The following guide provides the anticipated round-by-round schedule based on the tournament dates and 32-player singles draw.<\/p>\r\n\r\n<h2 data-section-id=\"cfooi\" data-start=\"1468\" data-end=\"1513\">2026 ATP China Open Tournament Information<\/h2>\r\n<p data-start=\"1515\" data-end=\"1846\"><strong data-start=\"1515\" data-end=\"1530\">Tournament:<\/strong> China Open<br data-start=\"1541\" data-end=\"1544\"><strong data-start=\"1544\" data-end=\"1554\">Dates:<\/strong> September 30\u2013October 6, 2026<br data-start=\"1583\" data-end=\"1586\"><strong data-start=\"1586\" data-end=\"1599\">Location:<\/strong> Beijing, China<br data-start=\"1614\" data-end=\"1617\"><strong data-start=\"1617\" data-end=\"1627\">Venue:<\/strong> National Tennis Center<br data-start=\"1650\" data-end=\"1653\"><strong data-start=\"1653\" data-end=\"1666\">Category:<\/strong> ATP 500<br data-start=\"1674\" data-end=\"1677\"><strong data-start=\"1677\" data-end=\"1689\">Surface:<\/strong> Outdoor hard court<br data-start=\"1708\" data-end=\"1711\"><strong data-start=\"1711\" data-end=\"1728\">Singles Draw:<\/strong> 32 players<br data-start=\"1739\" data-end=\"1742\"><strong data-start=\"1742\" data-end=\"1759\">Doubles Draw:<\/strong> 16 teams<br data-start=\"1768\" data-end=\"1771\"><strong data-start=\"1771\" data-end=\"1802\">Defending Singles Champion:<\/strong> Jannik Sinner<br data-start=\"1816\" data-end=\"1819\"><strong data-start=\"1819\" data-end=\"1835\">Prize Money:<\/strong> $4,089,385<\/p>\r\n\r\n<h2 data-section-id=\"1bfj8xw\" data-start=\"1848\" data-end=\"1898\">Wednesday, September 30: ATP First Round Begins<\/h2>\r\n<p data-start=\"1900\" data-end=\"2035\">The opening day of the ATP China Open is expected to feature first-round singles and doubles matches across the National Tennis Center.<\/p>\r\n<p data-start=\"2037\" data-end=\"2237\">With only 32 places in the singles draw, every player will begin one victory away from the round of 16. There are no opening-round byes, meaning the leading seeds must be ready from their first match.<\/p>\r\n<p data-start=\"2239\" data-end=\"2471\">The schedule could feature several unseeded dangers, including Andrey Rublev, Alexander Bublik, Jakub Mensik, Hubert Hurkacz and Cameron Norrie. Their presence makes the draw considerably more difficult than a typical ATP 500 event.<\/p>\r\n<p data-start=\"2473\" data-end=\"2494\"><strong data-start=\"2473\" data-end=\"2494\">Scheduled rounds:<\/strong><\/p>\r\n\r\n<ul data-start=\"2496\" data-end=\"2547\">\r\n \t<li data-section-id=\"1ik91oc\" data-start=\"2496\" data-end=\"2521\">ATP singles first round<\/li>\r\n \t<li data-section-id=\"1uecqab\" data-start=\"2522\" data-end=\"2547\">ATP doubles first round<\/li>\r\n<\/ul>\r\n<h2 data-section-id=\"16muwul\" data-start=\"2549\" data-end=\"2601\">Thursday, October 1: First-Round Action Continues<\/h2>\r\n<p data-start=\"2603\" data-end=\"2686\">The remaining first-round singles matches are expected to be completed on Thursday.<\/p>\r\n<p data-start=\"2934\" data-end=\"3171\">Djokovic will attract equal attention when he returns to the China Open for the first time since 2015. The Serbian is a six-time champion and has never lost at the tournament, carrying a perfect 29-0 Beijing record into the 2026 edition.<\/p>\r\n<p data-start=\"3173\" data-end=\"3194\"><strong data-start=\"3173\" data-end=\"3194\">Scheduled rounds:<\/strong><\/p>\r\n\r\n<ul data-start=\"3196\" data-end=\"3247\">\r\n \t<li data-section-id=\"1ik91oc\" data-start=\"3196\" data-end=\"3221\">ATP singles first round<\/li>\r\n \t<li data-section-id=\"1uecqab\" data-start=\"3222\" data-end=\"3247\">ATP doubles first round<\/li>\r\n<\/ul>\r\n<h2 data-section-id=\"1tf6gey\" data-start=\"3249\" data-end=\"3289\">Friday, October 2: Round of 16 Begins<\/h2>\r\n<p data-start=\"3291\" data-end=\"3422\">The tournament should move into the second round on Friday, when the top contenders begin facing increasingly dangerous opposition.<\/p>\r\n<p data-start=\"3424\" data-end=\"3642\">Potential matchups between seeded players and high-quality unseeded opponents could make this one of the most entertaining days of the opening week. The smaller draw means there is little protection for the favourites.<\/p>\r\n<p data-start=\"3796\" data-end=\"3817\"><strong data-start=\"3796\" data-end=\"3817\">Scheduled rounds:<\/strong><\/p>\r\n\r\n<ul data-start=\"3819\" data-end=\"3889\">\r\n \t<li data-section-id=\"1mclx06\" data-start=\"3819\" data-end=\"3845\">ATP singles second round<\/li>\r\n \t<li data-section-id=\"168fhhv\" data-start=\"3846\" data-end=\"3889\">ATP doubles first round and quarterfinals<\/li>\r\n<\/ul>\r\n<h2 data-section-id=\"13xgkkh\" data-start=\"3891\" data-end=\"3936\">Saturday, October 3: Round of 16 Continues<\/h2>\r\n<p data-start=\"3938\" data-end=\"4019\">The remaining singles quarterfinalists are expected to be determined on Saturday.<\/p>\r\n<p data-start=\"4021\" data-end=\"4337\">This stage often produces tactical contrasts between aggressive first-strike players and opponents who prefer to extend rallies. With Djokovic, Zverev, Auger-Aliassime, de Minaur and Medvedev entered, the tournament has the potential to deliver elite-level matchups before the weekend reaches its conclusion.<\/p>\r\n<p data-start=\"4339\" data-end=\"4360\"><strong data-start=\"4339\" data-end=\"4360\">Scheduled rounds:<\/strong><\/p>\r\n\r\n<ul data-start=\"4362\" data-end=\"4416\">\r\n \t<li data-section-id=\"1mclx06\" data-start=\"4362\" data-end=\"4388\">ATP singles second round<\/li>\r\n \t<li data-section-id=\"ab97q8\" data-start=\"4389\" data-end=\"4416\">ATP doubles quarterfinals<\/li>\r\n<\/ul>\r\n<h2 data-section-id=\"1dvecgm\" data-start=\"4418\" data-end=\"4465\">Sunday, October 4: ATP Singles Quarterfinals<\/h2>\r\n<p data-start=\"4467\" data-end=\"4526\">Sunday should feature all four men\u2019s singles quarterfinals.<\/p>\r\n<p data-start=\"4528\" data-end=\"4715\">The compact schedule will make physical recovery increasingly important. Players who require lengthy opening matches may have little time to recover before facing another Top 20 opponent.<\/p>\r\n<p data-start=\"4717\" data-end=\"4848\">The quarterfinals will also carry substantial implications for the late-season rankings and the race to qualify for the ATP Finals.<\/p>\r\n<p data-start=\"4850\" data-end=\"4871\"><strong data-start=\"4850\" data-end=\"4871\">Scheduled rounds:<\/strong><\/p>\r\n\r\n<ul data-start=\"4873\" data-end=\"4943\">\r\n \t<li data-section-id=\"8nsnnz\" data-start=\"4873\" data-end=\"4900\">ATP singles quarterfinals<\/li>\r\n \t<li data-section-id=\"1hzp752\" data-start=\"4901\" data-end=\"4943\">ATP doubles quarterfinals and semifinals<\/li>\r\n<\/ul>\r\n<h2 data-section-id=\"uci3it\" data-start=\"4945\" data-end=\"4989\">Monday, October 5: ATP Singles Semifinals<\/h2>\r\n<p data-start=\"4991\" data-end=\"5077\">The final four will compete for places in the China Open championship match on Monday.<\/p>\r\n<p data-start=\"5079\" data-end=\"5301\">A semifinal Djokovic would be one of the most anticipated moments of the Asian Swing. Zverev, Medvedev, Auger-Aliassime and de Minaur will each have legitimate ambitions of reaching this stage as well.<\/p>\r\n<p data-start=\"5303\" data-end=\"5442\">At this point in the tournament, the ability to protect second serves and convert limited break-point opportunities should become decisive.<\/p>\r\n<p data-start=\"5444\" data-end=\"5465\"><strong data-start=\"5444\" data-end=\"5465\">Scheduled rounds:<\/strong><\/p>\r\n\r\n<ul data-start=\"5467\" data-end=\"5516\">\r\n \t<li data-section-id=\"1ey8r3d\" data-start=\"5467\" data-end=\"5491\">ATP singles semifinals<\/li>\r\n \t<li data-section-id=\"1ppo6g6\" data-start=\"5492\" data-end=\"5516\">ATP doubles semifinals<\/li>\r\n<\/ul>\r\n<h2 data-section-id=\"n5uv8v\" data-start=\"5518\" data-end=\"5562\">Tuesday, October 6: ATP China Open Finals<\/h2>\r\n<p data-start=\"5564\" data-end=\"5654\">The 2026 ATP China Open concludes with the men\u2019s singles and doubles championship matches.<\/p>\r\n<p data-start=\"5656\" data-end=\"5876\">Djokovic could pursue an extraordinary seventh Beijing title. Zverev is seeking his first China Open championship after reaching three previous semifinals.<\/p>\r\n<p data-start=\"5878\" data-end=\"6009\">The singles champion will receive 500 ATP ranking points and one of the most prestigious trophies available during the Asian Swing.<\/p>\r\n<p data-start=\"6011\" data-end=\"6032\"><strong data-start=\"6011\" data-end=\"6032\">Scheduled rounds:<\/strong><\/p>\r\n\r\n<ul data-start=\"6034\" data-end=\"6073\">\r\n \t<li data-section-id=\"t61ow8\" data-start=\"6034\" data-end=\"6053\">ATP singles final<\/li>\r\n \t<li data-section-id=\"lxhpt3\" data-start=\"6054\" data-end=\"6073\">ATP doubles final<\/li>\r\n<\/ul>\r\n<h2 data-section-id=\"lhx9wh\" data-start=\"6075\" data-end=\"6130\">When Will the ATP Beijing Order of Play Be Released?<\/h2>\r\n<p data-start=\"6132\" data-end=\"6308\">The detailed order of play is normally published after the conclusion of matches on the preceding day. It will include confirmed matchups, court assignments and starting times.<\/p>\r\n<p data-start=\"6310\" data-end=\"6462\">Beijing operates on China Standard Time, which is <strong data-start=\"6360\" data-end=\"6369\">UTC+8<\/strong>.
